_what: This catalogue's own prose is written in English, and a language check over the artefact is the natural way to keep it so. But three entries will fail that check forever and must never be 'fixed', because their only non-English words are a quotation. Written 2026-11-25, when a count of French entries came back as 15 and the real defect was 12.
_the_three_entries: brands/cambridge (`_the_robots_signal_and_the_decision_on_it`), brands/shanling (`_cleared_to_harvest_on_the_product_host`), and vocabulary/sources-and-redistribution (`_REGISTER_OF_REFUSALS._USE_REFERENCE_IS_PERMISSION_decided_2026_11_25`). Every one is English apart from four words: « C'est reference. » Those are the project owner's own words, recorded verbatim as the authority for the decision that a Content-Signal of « ai-train=no, use=reference » is this project's permission to read a page.
_the_rule: A quotation keeps the language it was spoken or written in. Translating « C'est reference. » into « It's reference. » would not clean up prose: it would falsify the record of who decided what, in what words. The same holds for every `source.quote` in the base, and for any clause quoted from a maker's terms page - a German or Japanese prohibition is quoted as written, not rendered into English.
_so_a_language_guard_must_exempt: Text inside guillemets, every `source.quote`, and any field whose value is an attributed quotation. What it should measure is the catalogue's OWN prose, and it must find that prose by WALKING every string in the entry - not by consulting a list of field names. A named list is the same mistake one level up: it is current only until the next note field is invented, and it would miss a `policy._this_is_a_policy` the day someone writes one. Walk keys as well as values. Keys matter and are easy to forget - on 2026-11-25 a detector that read only values missed four French keys on brands/xduoo, one each on aune-audio, musetec-audio, yulong-audio and both bryston records, while reporting the base clean.
_and_two_traps_in_the_word_list: English-ambiguous words inflate the count: « decision », « conditions », « signal », « non », « LA » (from the LA-QXD1 model name) and « AUX » (a connector) each produced a false positive, between them turning a true 12 into a reported 15. A guard should print the words it matched, not only a score, so that a reader can tell a defect from a model number. A count alone cannot be checked, and a wrong one was twice used to contradict a correct report.
